title: Relative cone extension with explicit biproduct terms
statement: Let A be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. Let E,H,Q be integer-indexed cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], f:E→H and r:Q→Cone(f), with r a quasi-isomorphism [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. Assume E and Q bounded above, possibly by different integers. There are a bounded-above complex F and maps t:E→F, g:F→H, with g a quasi-isomorphism, t≫g=f, every t^i split mono, and F^i isomorphic to E^i⊕Q^i. No generator, flatness, boundedness of H, or surjectivity assumption is needed.

source.place: Relative cone triangle before the final termwise-surjectivity addition; explicit coordinate proof adapted from the proved RelativeFlatExtension module.

proof.text: Extract the degree-one component a_i:Q^i→E^{i+1} and degree-zero component b_i:Q^i→H^i of r. Its chain-map equations are a_i d_E + d_Q a_{i+1}=0 and d_Q b_{i+1}=a_i f_{i+1}+b_i d_H. Construct F^i=E^i⊕Q^i with differential whose diagonal is (d_E,d_Q) and off-diagonal is -a_i. Biprod extensionality and these equations prove square-zero. The inclusion t and map g=(f,b) are chain maps; t≫g=f and t is split by the first projection. The maximum of the bounds bounds F. The term isomorphisms are identities.

Construct a degreewise three-summand permutation isomorphism Cone(g)≅Cone(r), using the explicit cone inclusions and projections. The same two component equations verify compatibility with differentials. Since r is a quasi-isomorphism, Cone(r) is acyclic. Transport its zero homology across this complex isomorphism, and apply the acyclic-cone characterization to g.

mathlib_searches.query: Given a quasi-isomorphism Q to the mapping cone of f E to H in an abelian category construct a quasi-isomorphism E direct sum Q to H extending f and a degreewise split inclusion of E
A resolution of the mapping cone of f gives a quasi-isomorphism from a twisted direct sum with a degreewise split inclusion of the source
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits: cm5b.instQuasiIsoIntP, mappingCone.quasiIso_descShortComplex, mappingConeHomOfDegreewiseSplitIso, mappingConeHomOfDegreewiseSplitXIso, mappingConeHomOfDegreewiseSplitIso_hom_f, mappingCone.mapHomologicalComplexIso, cm5b.homotopyEquiv, and mappingCone.mapHomologicalComplexXIso. Read DegreewiseSplit and ShortExact: these identify cones of an already supplied split short exact sequence or compare its quotient; they do not construct the strict relative extension from a supplied cone resolution. CM5b uses enough injectives and provides a different factorization.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_relative_biprod_cone_extension
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C]
    (E H : CochainComplex C ℤ) (f : E ⟶ H)
    (hE : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero (E.X i))
    (Q : CochainComplex C ℤ) (r : Q ⟶ mappingCone f)
    (hQ : ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero (Q.X i)) (hr : QuasiIso r) :
    ∃ (F : CochainComplex C ℤ) (t : E ⟶ F) (g : F ⟶ H),
      (∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero (F.X i)) ∧
      QuasiIso g ∧ t ≫ g = f ∧ (∀ i : ℤ, IsSplitMono (t.f i)) ∧
      ∀ i : ℤ, Nonempty (F.X i ≅ E.X i ⊞ Q.X i)
